title: Verdant 38 — Cascades: Animated Waterfalls, Rapids, Tall Cliffs Tileset for RPG Maker MZ, Tiled, Godot & Unity [16x16]
shortText: Animated 16x16 waterfalls that stack to any cliff height, plus rapids and plunge pools. MZ, Tiled, Godot, Unity.

metadata.assetLicence: Commercial use permitted, unlimited projects, no attribution required, no resale of the pack

description:
Waterfalls you build on the 16x16 grid. A river crosses the upland, runs white through rapids, goes over the edge and falls down a cliff of any height into a plunge pool, and every piece of it is a tile that animates. 489 tiles in one 22-colour palette. Commercial use permitted in unlimited projects, no attribution required; you may not resell the tiles themselves as an asset pack.

What is in it

  • The fall column in 4 shapes (single, left, middle, right): one tile that repeats down the cliff with no seam, so a cliff is as tall as you paint it, and a river of any width gets a fall of the same width.
  • Lips where a river goes over the edge (over a tall cliff, or over Scarp's one-tile cliff), landings at the cliff foot, and plunge pools whose tile cuts the pool's bank so the white water runs straight in.
  • Rapids flowing north to south and west to east, on the upland or the meadow, with their banks.
  • 3 complete 47-mask sets (329 autotile tiles): water on the upland and water on the meadow, both animated, and the upland edge.
  • A tall cliff face: 4 rock variants that meet on every side, plus its top edge, ends, foot and a step where it meets a one-tile cliff (22 pieces).
  • 42 animations (126 animated tiles plus the animated water sets). Flowing water is a true loop, so it never runs backwards.
  • A finished 32x20 sample map with three falls, as PNG, JSON and a Tiled .tmx; tiles.json with every tile's role, frame order, timing and passability.

Where it animates

  • Tiled: every animation is written into the .tsx files. Tiled's own renderer drew the sample map at 12 points in time and matched our frames exactly (1,966,080 pixels).
  • RPG Maker MZ: the two water sets animate on the A1 page, and the fall column is MZ's own waterfall autotile (A1 kind 5): paint it and MZ picks the shape. Every shape was composed back out of the sheet with MZ's own tables (396 of 396 identical). Lips, landings, plunge pools and rapids are on the object pages, where MZ shows them still.
  • Godot 4: one TileSet with all 489 tiles, loaded and verified in Godot 4.7.2. The frames are separate tiles there, with no animation set up; tiles.json lists each animation's frames and timing.
  • Unity: drop the Unity folder into your project and run one menu command. It slices 489 pixel-exact sprites and makes 489 Tiles with collision, 42 AnimatedTiles, 3 RuleTile brushes (the two water sets animated) and a scene with the sample map. Tested in a blank Unity 6000.5.7f1 project: every RuleTile drew the right transition in all 256 neighbourhoods (768 of 768), Unity read back every animation's frames in order at the declared speed, and its render of the sample scene matched our map pixel for pixel. Needs the free 2D Tilemap Extras package for the brushes and AnimatedTiles; without it everything else still builds.

Works with the series

The meadow, the upland and its edge are Verdant 12 — Scarp's own tiles, byte for byte (55 of them), so the falls drop straight into a Scarp map, and this pack also works on its own. For coast, rivers and marsh in the same palette, see Verdant 04 — Tidewater.

The proofs

Every tile's wrap boundary is measured against its own interior, and every 4x4 repetition is rendered and reviewed. Grid, palette and autotile completeness are machine-proven: every tile is exactly 16x16, every pixel is inside the palette, and alpha is strictly on or off.

AI disclosure

Every tile is generated by our own procedural drawing engine, which is AI-written software. No image model, no scraped art and no training dataset were used, and nothing was traced.
